passage:
Daycare note, Tuesday. Ayesha.
When snack time ended, Darshan went stiff and red-faced and threw his cup. He tried to hit me too. I moved the cups away, knelt nearby and said, "You're so angry. I'll keep you safe." I didn't punish or lecture. I waited. After a few minutes he crawled into my lap. Then we cleaned up together.

qa.q: What did Darshan throw?
qa.a: Darshan threw his cup.

qa.q: What was Darshan feeling when snack time ended?
qa.a: Darshan was furious; his stiff body, red face and throwing show an anger he could not yet control.

qa.q: Why did Ayesha wait instead of punishing?
qa.a: A toddler cannot yet put the brakes on anger, so keeping him safe and staying calm lets the storm pass and teaches more than a punishment.

qa.q: What might Ayesha have felt when Darshan tried to hit?
qa.a: Ayesha may have felt startled, yet stayed steady and kept Darshan safe rather than taking it personally.

grounding: A toddler's fury shows as a stiff body, a red face, throwing and hitting, and is met with calm, safety and waiting rather than punishment.

passage: At the temple fair in their village, two-year-old Ritu wanted the red balloon and was told no. Her body went rigid, her face turned red, and she flung her slipper at the stall. An old man muttered, "One smack and she'll stop." Her mother, Vinita, only scooped her away from the busy lane, sat on the temple step and held her loosely. "You're so cross. I'm here." Ritu kicked and wailed, then slowly slumped against her.

qa.q: What did Ritu fling at the stall?
qa.a: Ritu flung her slipper at the stall.

qa.q: What was Ritu feeling when she was told no?
qa.a: Ritu was furious; her rigid body and red face show an anger she had no way yet to stop.

qa.q: Why was Vinita's response wiser than the old man's suggestion?
qa.a: Vinita kept Ritu safe from the busy lane and waited calmly, letting the anger pass instead of adding fear with a smack.

qa.q: How does the old man see Ritu's outburst?
qa.a: The old man sees it as naughtiness to be stopped with a smack, not as a small child overwhelmed by anger.

grounding: A toddler's anger shows as stiffness, a red face and throwing, and is handled by keeping the child safe, staying calm and waiting.

passage: The biscuit tin was empty. Two-year-old Hrithik went stiff, his face flaming red, and hurled his steel cup across the Kolkata kitchen. Then he flung himself on the floor, kicking. Deepak didn't shout. He moved the cup and the chairs out of reach and sat down nearby. 'You're so angry. I'm here.' Hrithik screamed and kicked. Deepak waited. Slowly the screams became sobs, and Hrithik crawled into his lap.

qa.q: What did Hrithik throw across the kitchen?
qa.a: His steel cup.

qa.q: What does Hrithik's stiff body and red face suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: He was furious and overwhelmed, too little to stop the anger once it started.

qa.q: What did Deepak do that helped?
qa.a: He stayed calm, kept Hrithik safe by moving things away, named the anger and waited nearby.

qa.q: What would change if Deepak had smacked or shouted?
qa.a: Hrithik would likely have got more upset, and he would not learn that big anger can be survived calmly.

grounding: Shows a toddler's fury bursting out as a stiff body, red face and throwing, and a calm adult keeping him safe and waiting instead of punishing.

passage:
'Time to go home, Karthik.'
'NO!'
'I know. You love the swings.'
Karthik's face went red. He hit Gautam's leg. 'NO GO!'
Gautam caught his small fist gently. 'I won't let you hit. You're very, very cross.'
Karthik threw himself on the sand, roaring.
Gautam sat down beside him. 'I'm here. I'll wait.'
A lady walking past frowned. Gautam stayed calm.
Karthik roared, then cried, then went quiet. He crept over and leaned on Gautam's arm.
'Ready? One last swing on the way?'
A sniffly nod.

qa.q: What does Karthik love at the park?
qa.a: The swings.

qa.q: What does Karthik's hitting and roaring show he was feeling?
qa.a: He was very angry and upset about leaving, and his body burst with it because he is too young to hold it in.

qa.q: How did Gautam keep Karthik safe without punishing him?
qa.a: He gently stopped the hitting, named the feeling, sat nearby and waited until the storm passed.

qa.q: How might the lady walking past have seen the scene?
qa.a: She may have judged it as a naughty child and a soft parent, not seeing that calm waiting was helping.

grounding: Shows a toddler's anger coming out as hitting and roaring, and a parent who stays calm, keeps everyone safe and waits instead of punishing.

passage:
Daycare note, Wednesday
At block time Mia knocked down Pankaj's tall tower. Pankaj went rigid, face bright red, and threw blocks at her. I moved Mia to the book corner and stood between Pankaj and the others. I didn't scold. I knelt and said, 'You're so angry. Your tower fell.' He screamed and threw two more at the wall. I waited, voice soft. Soon he fell against me, sobbing. We rebuilt the tower together. He's only two.
Thomas, room carer

qa.q: Who knocked Pankaj's tower down?
qa.a: Mia.

qa.q: What was Pankaj feeling when he went rigid and red?
qa.a: He was furious and heartbroken that his tower had been knocked down.

qa.q: Which of Thomas's choices protected everyone?
qa.a: Moving Mia away and standing between Pankaj and the others, while staying calm and waiting.

qa.q: How might Mia have felt when the blocks came at her?
qa.a: Mia was probably scared and upset, and moving to the book corner helped her feel safe.

grounding: Shows a toddler's fury as a rigid body, red face and throwing, and a carer keeping others safe, staying calm and waiting instead of punishing.

passage: In the courtyard of their house near Hubli, little Avni wanted the red bucket her cousin was holding. When she didn't get it, her whole body went stiff, her face turned red, and she flung her steel cup, then hit at Swati's legs. Swati didn't shout or smack. She moved the cup and the cousin out of reach, knelt nearby and waited, saying softly, 'You're so angry. I'm here.' Avni screamed, then sobbed, then crawled into her lap. After a while Swati said, 'Now shall we find you a bucket?'

qa.q: What did Avni want?
qa.a: The red bucket her cousin was holding.

qa.q: What was Avni feeling when her body went stiff?
qa.a: She was furious and frustrated, with no way yet to stop the anger, so it came out as throwing and hitting.

qa.q: What did Swati do instead of punishing?
qa.a: She kept everyone safe, stayed calm and close, named the anger softly and waited until Avni settled.

qa.q: How might the cousin have felt during the outburst?
qa.a: The cousin was probably startled and a little scared by the throwing and screaming.

grounding: A toddler's fury comes out as a stiff body, red face, throwing and hitting, and a calm adult keeps her safe and waits.
